records.title: Choroid plexus and paraphysis in lower vertebrates
records.query: In which vertebrate classes is a paraphysis present in the adult brain versus only in the embryo?
records.verified_via: wiley metadata (title, authors, journal); year and PMID confirmed in PubMed (lookup_article_by_citation + get_article_metadata)
records.excerpt: Based on a common neuroepithelial origin and similar histochemical properties, we conclude that the paraphysis is a modified choroid plexus. The *velum transversum* is an arbitrary boundary between diencephalon and telencephalon, and is itself formed of choroid plexus. The medial telencephalic ventricle is the rostral portion of the third ventricle. All neuroepithelial infoldings at the rostral end of the diencephalic roof including the *velum transversum* are intraventricular choroid plexuses; the neuroepithelial outpouchings in this region are the extraventricular choroid plexuses (paraphysis) of the diencephalon.
records.note: Comparative histology of third-ventricle choroid plexus and paraphysis in lower vertebrates; concludes the paraphysis is a modified (extraventricular) choroid plexus and that the velum transversum is an arbitrary boundary. [Wiley record has no publicationDate (citationLine 'n.d.'); year 1966 from PubMed.]

records.title: The histology of the paraphysis of Amblystoma
records.query: What do classical comparative anatomical studies describe about the paraphysis and the dorsal sac in the brains of fishes, amphibians and reptiles?
records.verified_via: wiley metadata (title, authors, journal, volume, pages); year absent in Wiley record and article not found in PubMed lookup
records.excerpt:
The paraphysis of adult Amblystoma is made up of low columnar ependymal epithelit m which forms the paraphyseal tubules which end blindly and which communicate with one another by a common mouth with the third ventricle. Between the paraphyseal tubules venous sinusoids anastomose freely with one another forming a complicated rete. The sinusoids are made up entirely of endothelium. The blood supply to the paraphysis is entirely venous.

Mitochondria were found in great abundance in the paraphysis of one female just previous to laying. Other specimens showed very few present.
records.note: Classical histology of the adult Amblystoma paraphysis: ependymal tubules opening by a common mouth into the third ventricle, with a sinusoidal venous rete. [No publicationDate in Wiley record (citationLine 'n.d.'); not found in PubMed lookup; year unconfirmed (J Morphol vol 59).]

records.title: Ultrastructure and organization of circumventricular organs and endolymphatic tubules in the treefrog, Hyla versicolor
records.authors: Kemnitz CP, Fox LM, McNulty JA
records.query: Is the paraphysis cerebri homologous to the telencephalic choroid plexus or to the dorsal sac of the vertebrate brain?
records.excerpt: The morphology and anatomical relationship of the paraphysis, anterior choroid plexus, and endolymphatic tubules of *Hyla versicolor* suggest that these structures may act as a functional unit to regulate composition of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Ependymal cells of both the paraphysis and the choroid plexus exhibit ultrastructural features (an extensive microvillar border, large intercellular spaces containing an amorphous material, and apically located mitochondria) which indicate active exchange between the blood and CSF. Mast cells (which may play a role in regulating vascular permeability) also occur on the brush border.
records.note: Treefrog (Hyla versicolor) paraphysis, anterior choroid plexus and endolymphatic tubules interpreted as one functional unit regulating CSF composition.

records.title: The pineal‐paraphyseal complex of sea turtles. I. Light microscopic description
records.query: In reptiles such as lizards, turtles and snakes, how do the paraphysis, the dorsal sac and the pineal complex relate to each other on the roof of the forebrain?
records.excerpt: The paraphysis is extensively fused to the distal portion of the pineal body, suggesting an interrelated function for these two tissues. No duct or canal was observed connecting the pineal lumen to the third ventricle. Two pineal cell types are described which appear to correspond to the neuroglial supportive cells and the secretory rudimentary photoreceptor cells of other amniotic vertebrates. A possible luminal secretion in the form of apical protrusions is produced by the latter cell type. No typical photoreceptive outer segments were observed.
records.note: Sea turtle (Chelonia, Caretta) pineal-paraphyseal complex: large dorsally projecting structure with the paraphysis fused to the distal pineal; several age classes examined.

records.title: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis cerebri of the water snake Natrix maura L
records.authors: Fernández-Llebrez P, Becerra J, Marín-Girón F
records.query: Where is the paraphysis located relative to the velum transversum and the choroid plexus of the third ventricle in the amphibian brain?
records.excerpt: Paraphyseal epithelial cells of *Natrix maura* have been studied with light and electron microscopy. They showed a clear polarity apically related to the third ventricle and, basally, to a connective tissue layer which surrounded the whole organ. The apical surface of the cells, attached by junctional complexes, showed many microvilli, scarce cilia, and some pinocytotic coated vesicles. In their apical cytoplasm many mitochondria and a well developed Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum were observed. Whereas lamellar bodies were abundant and closely related with mitochondria, glycogen particles were absent.
records.note: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis cerebri of the water snake Natrix maura (apical microvilli, coated vesicles, junctional complexes).

records.title: Ultrastructure of the paraphysis in Bufo bufo larvae
records.authors: Farnesi RM, Tei S, Vagnetti D, Santarella B, Pollacci P
records.query: Where is the paraphysis located relative to the velum transversum and the choroid plexus of the third ventricle in the amphibian brain?
records.excerpt: A study of the ultrastructure and function of the paraphysis in *Bufo bufo* larvae was carried out. The structure is a tubularramified gland made up of numerous tubules with monolayered epithelial walls surrounded by connective tissue and sinusoids. The epithelial cells secrete glycoprotein to contribute to production of the cephalorachidian fluid. The role of the paraphysis in the transport of fluids and electrolytes from the blood to the cephalorachidian fluid in regulation of ionic and osmotic homeostasis is discussed.  1994 WileyLiss, Inc.
records.note: Ultrastructure and secretory function of the paraphysis in Bufo bufo larvae: tubular-ramified gland secreting glycoprotein into the cephalorachidian fluid.

records.title: Occurrence of bone fractures and parathyroid hyperplasia in paraphysectomized frogs (Rana catesbeiana)
records.authors: Nelson SR, Foltz FM, Camarata P, Sarras MP
records.query: Is the paraphysis present in the brain of anurans (frogs and toads) and caecilians, and how does it vary among the amphibian orders?
records.excerpt: The physiological role of the amphibian paraphysis was studied by removing the paraphysis from bullfrog tadpoles (*Rana catesbeiana*) and observing change in frog weight, bone development, and parathyroid glands 22 months later. Development was similar in control and paraphysectomized frogs until 6 months when the experimental frogs began to show greater weight gain which persisted for the remaining 16 months. At the time of sacrifice (22 months after paraphysectomy), the parathyroid glands of the experimental frogs were enlarged with a tenfold increase in wet weight and a sevenfold increase in dry weight.
records.note: Paraphysectomy in bullfrog tadpoles: altered weight gain, bone development and parathyroids 22 months later (physiological role of the amphibian paraphysis).

records.title: An enigmatic eye: the histology of the tuatara pineal complex
records.query: In reptiles such as lizards, turtles and snakes, how do the paraphysis, the dorsal sac and the pineal complex relate to each other on the roof of the forebrain?
records.excerpt:
The paraphysis is an evagination from the *lamina supraneuroporica* of the telencephalon[^13^](#b13). It appears to have a secretory function although little research has been carried out examining its biochemistry[^15^](#b15). It has numerous lumens and originally opened into the third ventricle, but Dendy demonstrated that the opening shifts to above the *commissura aberrans* during embryologic development, such that it opens into the dorsal sac[^13^](#b13).

The dorsal sac is an outpouching from the third ventricle and retains this connection. The dorsal sac contains choroid plexus with a structure identical to that of the choroid plexus of the lateral ventricles.
records.note: Tuatara pineal complex histology: paraphysis defined as an evagination of the lamina supraneuroporica, lying caudal to the pineal eye and rostral to the dorsal sac / pineal sac.

records.title: The dorsal sack, the aulix and the diencephalic flexure
records.query: In which vertebrate classes is a paraphysis present in the adult brain versus only in the embryo?
records.verified_via: wiley metadata (title, author, journal, volume, pages); Wiley publicationDate/citation gives implausible year 2032, not in PubMed lookup
records.excerpt: In many of the lower vertebrates there is a pouchlike evagination of the diatela (membranous roof of the diacele, or "third ventricle") between the epiphysis and the paraphysis. In *Ceratodus* and in *Polyodon* it is anteverted and very large. In the green turtle it projects dorsad. Its mammalian representative is crowded caudad by the cerebrum and rests upon the retroverted epiphysis. It is commonly ignored in figures and descriptions, but was shown by Reichert. The speaker, without recognizing its homology, figured it in the *New York Medical Journal*, 1885, p. 320. It is large in the sheep and long in the cow and horse. The diaplexuses are continued into it.
records.note: Early note defining the dorsal sack as a pouch of the diatela between epiphysis and paraphysis (large in Ceratodus and Polyodon, dorsad in turtle, caudad in mammals); terminology of the dorsal sac. [Wiley publicationDate '08 July 2032' is implausible (J Comp Neurol vol 6); true year unconfirmed.]

records.excerpt:
The paraphysis, which has probably a glandular function in some of the lower vertebrates, is not represented in the brain of the placental mammal.

The velum transversum and dorsal sac give rise to the choroid plexuses of the lateral and third ventricles. The arrangement of the choroid plexus of the third ventricle, the relationships of the dorsal sac and the histological appearances of these structures are described.

records.title: Spatiotemporal Patterns of Pax3, Pax6, and Pax7 Expression in the Developing Brain of a Urodele Amphibian, Pleurodeles waltl
records.authors: Joven A, Morona R, González A, Moreno N
records.query: Is the paraphysis a telencephalic derivative or a derivative of the diencephalic roof according to the prosomeric model of forebrain organisation?
records.excerpt: Thus, our present results suggest that the paraphysis is a roof plate derivative that originates at the limit between p3 and the evaginated telencephalon, more likely belonging to the first one. In the modified prosomeric model the paraphysis was disregarded, and the choroid plexus was the only derivative considered from the roof plate of p3 and telencephalon (Puelles and Rubenstein, [2003](#cne23385-bib-0180)).
records.note: Pax3/6/7 expression in developing Pleurodeles: paraphysis interpreted as roof-plate derivative at the p3/evaginated-telencephalon limit; discussion also places the large urodele paraphysis rostral to the velum transversum.

records.title: Expression patterns of Pax6 and Pax7 in the adult brain of a urodele amphibian, Pleurodeles waltl
records.authors: Joven A, Morona R, González A, Moreno N
records.query: In which vertebrate classes is a paraphysis present in the adult brain versus only in the embryo?
records.excerpt: The nature of the paraphysis (par), the structure that evaginates from the ventricle, is controversial. For some authors, this constitutes a telencephalic derivative, whereas for others it belongs to the roof of p3. Specifically in amphibians, it has been described as a posterior telencephalic organ adjacent to the choroid plexus of the third ventricle (ArinsKappers, [1956](#bib6)), but unlike the plexus it lacks the uptake mechanisms for cerebrospinal fluid (Jansen and Diederen, [1987](#bib91)). In urodeles a type of arginine vasotocin receptor was observed in the paraphysis, related to the osmotic and/or ionic regulation of the cerebrospinal fluid (Hasunuma et al., [2010](#bib81)).
records.note: Adult Pleurodeles Pax6/Pax7 atlas; notes that the nature of the paraphysis (telencephalic derivative vs roof of p3) is controversial.

records.title: Telencephalic morphogenesis during the process of neurulation: An experimental study using quail–chick chimeras
records.query: Is the paraphysis cerebri homologous to the telencephalic choroid plexus or to the dorsal sac of the vertebrate brain?
records.excerpt:
The velum transversum presumably limits at the roof of the prosomer 3 (p3) from the prosomer 2 (p2), and the paraphysis lies in p3.

The presumptive territory of the pallium covered the dorsal part of the secondary prosencephalon and extends 240 m in the mediolateral axis and 130 m in the anteroposterior axis in a dorsal view of the embryo. Thus, the territory of the prospective pallium reported by Cobos et al. ([2001b](#bib9)) in the neural plate has almost tripled its size in the mediolateral dimension after neural tube closure, whereas the rostrocaudal dimension maintained a similar size.
records.note: Quail-chick chimera fate mapping of the telencephalic roof: velum transversum at the p3/p2 roof limit and the paraphysis located in p3.

records.excerpt: The paraphysis cerebri is a glandular organ developed in amphibians and nonavian reptiles at the level of the 3rd ventricle (Hinton etal. [1990](#joa12613-bib-0027)). Variations in the size of the paraphysis cerebri are evident among the climberjumper *Hypsiboas pulchellus* (Fig.[6](#joa12613-fig-0006)D) and the climberwalkers *P.sauvagii* and *P.boliviana*, being bigger in the latter two species (Fig.[6](#joa12613-fig-0006)E,F), and less developed and cordonlike in the hopperwalker *R. fernandezae* (Fig.[6](#joa12613-fig-0006)C).

records.title: Agnathan brain anatomy and craniate phylogeny
records.authors: Khonsari RH, Li B, Vernier P, Northcutt RG, Janvier P
records.query: How is the paraphysis described in the brain of cyclostomes (lampreys and hagfishes)?
records.excerpt:
**93. Paraphysis (absent=0, present=1)**

The epithalamus is formed by the habenular nucleus and two diverticula  a left paraphysis (or parietal) and a right epiphysis (or pineal). Lampreys display both neural diverticula but chondrichthyans have retained only the right, pineal one, whereas actinopterygians and sarcopterygians exhibit both organs.

Surprisingly, hagfishes do not show any trace of a pineal organ, although a topological homologue of the habenular nucleus is described.

The left habenular nucleus and left fasciculus retroflexus are larger than the right ones in all craniates.

**94.
records.note: Craniate character matrix (char. 93 'Paraphysis'); here the left epithalamic diverticulum is called 'paraphysis (or parietal)' vs the right epiphysis, a terminological usage different from the telencephalic paraphysis; lampreys have both, chondrichthyans only the pineal.

records.title: Microvascularization of the pineal gland in the freshwater turtle, Pseudemys scripta elegans (Reptilia): A scanning electron microscopic study of vascular corrosion casts
records.query: Is the paraphysis cerebri homologous to the telencephalic choroid plexus or to the dorsal sac of the vertebrate brain?
records.excerpt: **Abstract: ** Gross supply, microvascular patterns, and drainage routes of the pineal gland and its vascular relations with associated structures (dorsal sac, paraphysis, choroid plexus of the third ventricle) were studied by scanning electron microscopy of microvascular corrosion casts in 10 specimens of the freshwater turtle, *Pseudemys scripta elegans*. Light microscopy of tissue sections (one transverse and one longitudinal series) served to attribute cast vascular territories to anatomical structures. The tubular pineal gland body is supplied bilaterally by small branches of the saccular artery, a branch of the lateral choroidal artery.
records.note: Turtle (Pseudemys) pineal microvasculature and its vascular relations with dorsal sac, paraphysis and third-ventricle choroid plexus.

records.title: Morphogenesis of Lateral Choroid Plexus During Human Embryonic Period

records.excerpt: The CP of the DV and paraphysis may arise around the JB because the CP of LV and DV are continuous in the mammalian brain (Netsky and Shuangshoti, [1975](#ar22662-bib-0018); Dziegielewska et al., [2001](#ar22662-bib-0005)). O'Rahilly and Mller ([1990](#ar22662-bib-0021)) observed it at CS18 for the first time. In this study, the primordium faces both LV and DV at CS 20. Paraphysis was detected at least after CS19 at the roof of the DV and the epithelium became thin and irregular around that, whereas the stroma remained undifferentiated. This study did not determine whether structures around the paraphysis were CP of the DV or part of the paraphysis.

records.excerpt: The arterial supply is from the dorsal mesencephalic artery via: (1) the ventral choroidal arteries (left and right); (2) the dorsal choroidal arteries (left and right); (3) the caudal choroidal arteries (left and right; (4) the ventral arteries of the dorsal sac; and, from the olfactory arteries, via 5) the rostral choroidal arteries. The venous drainage is mainly through a single main choroidal vein that can take various courses either directly to the anterior cardinal vein or via the middle cerebral vein to the anterior cardinal vein. To a lesser extent, the plexus is drained via the lateral telencephalic veins and the ventral vein of the dorsal sac to the middle cerebral vein.

records.excerpt: Colloid cyst epithelium, choroid plexus epithelium and ependyma showed different immunohistochemical profiles. In particular, antibodies to different cytokeratins and to transthyretin revealed considerable and constant differences of immunoreactivity. Therefore, common derivation of the three tissues seems unlikely. Our findings are interpreted in favour of the nonneuroepithelial origin of third ventricular colloid cysts.
records.note: Immunohistochemistry of 11 colloid cysts: cyst epithelium differs from choroid plexus epithelium and ependyma, questioning a common derivation.

records.title: Benign cysts in the central nervous system: Neuropathological observations of the cyst walls
records.query: Where is the paraphysis located relative to the velum transversum and the choroid plexus of the third ventricle in the amphibian brain?
records.excerpt: Colloid cysts in the third ventricle are wellknown entities, but their origins remain obscure. They are most often small and are often found incidentally at autopsy in the midline of the brain near the foramen of Monro. There are no known histological differences between incidental colloid cysts found at autopsy and those with symptoms requiring surgery. As the name implies, the cysts contain colloidlike material, which is heterogeneous and stains with almost all commonly used neuropathogical techniques. Because the cysts are located deep within the brain, they are surrounded by CNS tissue. They are sharply bordered oval masses just below the fornix of the septum pellucidum.
records.note: Neuropathology review of CNS benign cyst walls; comments that the origin of third-ventricle colloid cysts remains obscure.

records.title: Symptomatic neuroepithelial (colloid) cysts of the third ventricle. A unique case report in nontwin brothers
records.authors: Bengtson BP, Hedeman LS, Bauserman SC
records.query: What is the evidence that colloid cysts of the third ventricle originate from the paraphysis rather than from the choroid plexus or from endoderm?
records.excerpt: Much controversy remains as to the true cells of origin and pathogenesis of these cysts. Although a neuroepithelial origin has become increasingly accepted, Rathke cleft cysts, ectopic respiratory tissue, and other endodermal sources have been postulated. The first familial occurrence in middleaged identical twin brothers was cited recently in the literature. Described here are the first reports of symptomatic colloid cysts in two nontwin brothers, lending further support to the potential for genetic expression of neuroepithelial cysts.
records.note: Case report of colloid cysts in brothers; notes controversy about cell of origin and a neuroepithelial origin gaining acceptance.

records.title: Colloid cyst of the third ventricle: Cytomorphologic features on stereotactic fine‐needle aspiration
records.authors: Parwani AV, Fatani IY, Burger PC, Erozan YS, Ali SZ
records.query: What is the evidence that colloid cysts of the third ventricle originate from the paraphysis rather than from the choroid plexus or from endoderm?
records.excerpt: Colloid cyst (CC) is a rare nonneoplastic lesion thought to arise from misplaced endodermal tissue in the anterosuperior portion of the third ventricle. This study summarizes cytomorphologic features of CC on FNA along with clinical, radiologic, and histopathologic correlation. Ten cases of CC of the third ventricle diagnosed on FNA were retrospectively reviewed for a period of 12 yr (19892000). Material was obtained under stereotactic radiologic guidance. Smears were stained with DiffQuik and Papanicolaou stains and cell block sections with hematoxylin and eosin. The aspirates showed a characteristic sticky and viscous quality on gross examination.
records.note: Colloid cyst cytomorphology on stereotactic fine-needle aspiration; states the endodermal-misplacement view of origin.

records.title: Ventricular system and choroid plexuses of the human brain during the embryonic period proper

records.excerpt: After the appearance of the optic ventricle at stage 11, the cavity of the telencephalon medium is discernible at stage 13. At stage 14 the future cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles begin, and the rhomboid fossa becomes apparent. The medial and lateral ventricular eminences cause indentations in the lateral ventricle by stage 15. The hypothalamic sulcus is evident at stage 16. At stages 1718 the interventricular foramina are becoming relatively smaller, and cellular accumulations indicate the future choroid villi of the fourth and lateral ventricies.
records.note: Human embryonic ventricular system and choroid plexuses (Carnegie stages); describes the cavity of the telencephalon medium and early plexus indentation.

records.title: Towards a Terminologia Neuroanatomica
records.authors: Ten Donkelaar HJ, Broman J, Neumann PE, Puelles L, Riva A, Tubbs RS, Kachlik D

records.excerpt: The rostral border of D1 was defined as the rostral border of the chiasmatic plate, so as to include the eye vesicle in D1, and T (Telencephalon medium) as the part rostral to D1. D1 and T roughly correspond to the secondary prosencephalon (Fig. [2](#ca22809-fig-0002)). In the revised version of the TE and in the TNA, the prosomeric model developed by Luis Puelles and John Rubinstein (Fig. [3](#ca22809-fig-0003)) was adopted. Given the current state of knowledge, a system entailing neuromeres is a good working descriptor for use in organizing the terminology of the developing CNS and a reasonable framework for encompassing the current state of knowledge; also for the adult brain.
records.note: Terminologia Neuroanatomica proposal using the prosomeric model; defines telencephalon medium relative to D1 (secondary prosencephalon).

records.excerpt: The rostralmost (prechordal) forebrain is designated the secondary prosencephalon that contains the hypothalamus (rostral to the diencephalic p3), the telencephalon impar, and the telencephalic hemispheres (Puelles and Rubenstein,[2003](#bib133)). The interpretation of the parts of the secondary prosencephalon is fraught with difficulties, mainly derived from the early optic and hemispheric evaginations and the different degree of development shown across vertebrates that disturb the primary pattern of this region (Nieuwenhuys et al.,[2008](#bib121)).
records.note: Xenopus hypothalamus development paper stating the secondary prosencephalon contains hypothalamus, telencephalon impar and hemispheres.

records.excerpt: However, both the pallium and subpallium are usually held to reach the hemispheric stalk region, where they are continuous either with the telencephalic commissures or with preoptic, peduncular and eminentia thalami regions of the nonevaginated forebrain (the telencephalon impar of some authors). records.excerpt: Thus, in actinopterygii, a thin epitheliallike tissue, the tela choroidea (tc), covers the dorsal surface of the telencephalon (Figure[1c,d](#ede12474-fig-0001)). The degree of eversion varies between different species, so the taeniae (Figure[1cd](#ede12474-fig-0001)), that is, the places of attachment of the tc, are good landmarks for determining the degree of eversion (Nieuwenhuys,[1962](#ede12474-bib-0034),[2009b](#ede12474-bib-0037),[2011](#ede12474-bib-0038)).

records.title: Head size constrains forebrain development and evolution in ray‐finned fishes
records.query: What happened to the paraphysis during the evolution of the eversion of the telencephalon in ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii)?
records.excerpt: Over time, this dorsally directed thickening amplifies the initial laterally directed splaying of the dorsal telencephalic walls, stretches the telencephalic roof until it becomes an extremely thin *tela choroidea*, and produces the fullblown eversion typical of adult rayfinned fish telencephalons. Toward the end of embryonic development, the telencephalon becomes more elongated, such that only the olfactory bulbs remain lodged between the two olfactory epithelia and the caudal telencephalon ends up between the eyes ([Fig. 7H](#f7)). At these late stages of development, intracranial space is plentiful and the earlier proximity of brain, nasal epithelia, and eyes is no longer apparent.
records.note: Eversion of the telencephalon in ray-finned fishes: roof plate thins into a tela choroidea; head size as a developmental constraint.

Of these, a homology of the pineal organ, or epiphysis, between lampreys and sharks was recently confirmed (Lagadec *etal*. [2015](#dgd12347-bib-0035)). However, the brain of the hagfish stands in striking contrast to those of other vertebrates (Fig.[1](#dgd12347-fig-0001)E,F).

records.excerpt: The epiphysis develops into an organ complex (the parietal organ) with a dorsal component, the pineal eye or parietal eye, and a ventral component, the parapineal organ ([Fig. 19](#f19)) ([Tretjakoff, 1915](#b127)). [Dendy (1907)](#b20) considered these dorsal and ventral organs to be primitively paired right and left pineal eyes', respectively. Both contain putative photoreceptors in adults ([GarciaFernandez *et al.*, 1997](#b35); reviewed by [MelendezFerro *et al.*, 2002](#b89)). However, the parapineal develops later than the pineal, so that only the pineal contains opsinimmunoreactive photoreceptors during the larval period ([MelendezFerro *et al.*, 2002](#b89)).

records.excerpt: The development of CVOs has studied in detail in zebrafish, including the third and fourth ventricle CPs (CPIII and CPIV) (Bill et al.,[2008](#ca23994-bib-0016); Bill & Korzh,[2014](#ca23994-bib-0017); GarcaLecea et al.,[2008](#ca23994-bib-0058)), PIN (Masai et al.,[1997](#ca23994-bib-0117)), PP (Concha & Wilson,[2001](#ca23994-bib-0035)), NH and ME (Bassi et al.,[2016](#ca23994-bib-0012)), SCO (FernndezLlebrez et al.,[2001](#ca23994-bib-0055)), and AP (Ma,[1997](#ca23994-bib-0114)). records.title: The origins of the circumventricular organs
records.query: How did the dorsal midline circumventricular organs of vertebrates, such as the subcommissural organ, the pineal and the choroid plexus, evolve, and is the paraphysis considered a circumventricular organ?
records.excerpt: Here, I review our current knowledge of the embryonic development of the seven major CVOs (area postrema, median eminence, neurohypophysis, organum vasculosum of the lamina terminalis, pineal organ, subcommissural organ, subfornical organ) in embryos of different vertebrate species. Although there are conspicuous similarities between subsets of CVOs, no unifying feature characteristic of their development has been identified. Crossspecies comparisons suggest that CVOs also display a high degree of evolutionary flexibility.
records.note: Review of embryonic origins of circumventricular organs across vertebrates; context for dorsal-midline secretory organs.

records.excerpt:
So, as the lack of coronet cells and developmental location seem to rule out homology between the neural gland and the saccus vasculosus, could the neural gland be homologous to the vertebrate choroid plexus?

Ontogenetic evidence is consistent with homology between the neural gland and the CP. In the order Enterogona, in which the species studied are thought to have retained ancestral characters ([Berrill, 1948, 1950](#b47 #b48); [Svane, 1982](#b44)), the neural gland has been described, by all authors, including [Willey (1893](#b12)), as developing dorsally to the larval CNS ([Takamura, 2002](#b49); [Chiba *etal*., 2004](#b50)), from the larval ciliated duct ([Manni *etal*., 2005](#b51)).

Analyses of series of transverse sections of the brain showed the left medial habenular nucleus to be subdivided into pars dorsolateralis and pars ventromedialis, and the right medial habenular nucleus not to be so subdivided. The deepestdwelling of the forms studied, *Parvilux ingens*, showed a significant increase in the mean number of lamellar membranes in the outer segments of the receptor cells and a higher convergence ratio of receptor cells to ganglion cells as compared to the shallowdwelling form *Tarletonbeania crenularis*.

records.title: Two Intracranial Ligaments Supporting the Brain of the Brachiopterygian Fish Polypterus senegalus

records.excerpt: The former spans the orbitotemporal division of the cranial cavity and passes through the velum transversum. The latter, which is paired, extends from the roof to the sidewall of the endocranium and runs in the rhombomesencephalic sulcus in company with the trochlear nerve. It is argued that these intracranial ligments, like the spinal denticulate ligaments, are derivatives of a pair of fibrous bands which in early craniate phylogeny extended throughout the length of the neuraxial meninx and enhanced its tensile strength.
